A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 18-page versions of the same Sentence Smith paper. The main text, equations, Figures 1–5, Tables 1–9, and Appendix A support reliable comparison. Text and rendered-page comparisons identify only a version/date stamp update and a localized indexing correction.

before.justification: v3 reports original human evaluation of generated sentences, embedding-model experiments on PAWS and GPTP, and supplementary analyses in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including human assessments in Table 2, embedding evaluations in Tables 3–4 and 6–8, and manipulation-specific results in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The parsing, AMR manipulation, generation, NLI validation, and five manipulation rules are unchanged. The indexing correction below Equation (1) does not change the equation or the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English PAWS and GPTP paraphrase data and the same five semantic manipulation categories. No datasets, tasks, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated model sets are identical: the same 29 embeddings appear in Tables 3 and 6–8, and E5-Mistral and GTE-Qwen remain in Table 4. Comparator membership within each experiment is unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the greater-than-90% contradiction filter, the 50–80% neutral-filter ablation, TACC and AUC metrics, and the same aggregation procedures. Human evaluation still uses two annotators assessing 100 pairs from each dataset.

E4.justification: The manipulation-specific analysis, NLI-filtering ablation, MTEB ranking comparison, bag-of-words analysis, and appendix examples are identical. No analytical question or supporting evidence changes.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version adds run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the existing rank-correlation analyses are retained.

E6.justification: All numerical results, rankings, plotted findings, and example outputs are unchanged, including the appendices. For example, Table 3 reports sentence-t5-large at 0.9506 on PAWS, 0.8026 on GPTP, and 0.8704 in AVG in both PDFs.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the explanatory list from {t0, ...tn} to {t1, ..., tn}, matching Equation (1), which already begins with t1. This corrects notation without changing mathematical substance; no assumptions, derivations, or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about controllable, transparent sentence transformation, efficient generation, and fine-grained evaluation of text embeddings.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are identical, including the explanation for weaker large-model embeddings, AMR and English-language limitations, and the qualification that these rankings measure specific paraphrase phenomena rather than universal embedding quality.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, model identifiers, manipulation details, preprocessing instructions, and code/data/model access links are unchanged. The updated arXiv self-link only identifies the later document version.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and research positioning are identical, including comparisons with earlier semantic-graph approaches and concurrent LLM-generated hard-negative methods.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the transformation index and ellipsis punctuation below Equation (1). The first-page stamp changes from v3, 16 October 2025, to v4, 24 November 2025. All other prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–9 retain identical displays, captions, structures, and positions. Page organization is unchanged; the indexing edit causes only incidental line wrapping within its existing paragraph.

improvement.justification: v4 fixes a small indexing inconsistency below Equation (1), whose transformation sequence was already clear and unchanged. With the method, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and appendices otherwise identical, this editorial correction does not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
